notes: Describes the accepted LaunchToken, AdamDistributor and AdamTreasury sources in constructor dependency order. LaunchToken has no constructor arguments and sets name/symbol ADAM with 18 decimals. Policy $owner is the Treasury team beneficiary; no privileged wallet is hard-coded. Distributor excludedExtra is zero because no additional exclusion is configured and later contracts cannot be referenced. Treasury arguments match script/DeployAdam.s.sol: ETH/IMD pool fee 10000, spacing 200, no hook, 0 bps hook tax; ETH/PNKSTR pool fee 0, spacing 60, hook 0xfaaad5b731f52cdc9746f2414c823eca9b06e844, 1000 bps output-tax assumption; 1 ETH cap per buy leg, 300 bps slippage below the spot quote after fees and tax, 600-second process() cooldown. These reward-pool fees are unrelated to the launch pool fee. Anyone can call process(), for example hourly. New ETH is split 10% to $owner and 90% equally between the IMD and PNKSTR legs (odd wei to PNKSTR); after three days of continuous failure a leg's pending ETH can be rerouted to the other reward. Spot-derived minOut is not an independent price oracle or a guarantee against MEV. The accepted fork tests encode the pool and tax assumptions at block 26,126,549; this manifest is not a fresh onchain measurement. AdamHook is intentionally not a manifest contract. Its constructor calls Hooks.validateHookPermissions and reverts unless the deployed address has low 14 bits 0x20cc, which requires a mined CREATE2 salt; the factory deploys with supplied salts and this schema has no salt or mining field, so listing it would make the launch fail with 'project constructor failed' (reproduced: 0 of 32 unmined salts deploy). Neither Treasury nor Distributor takes the hook address and Treasury.receive() accepts ETH from any sender, so the factory deployment is complete without it. After launch the owner deploys AdamHook(PoolManager, ADAM, factory-deployed AdamTreasury, owner) through script/DeployAdam.s.sol step 4, which mines a salt with HookMiner for flags 0x20cc, then initializes the hooked PoolKey (ETH, ADAM, fee 0, spacing 60, AdamHook) and seeds it single-sided from the owner's own ADAM share as README steps 5 and 6. Only that hooked PoolKey takes the 1.5% ETH fee and the 20% to 1.5% anti-snipe decay. The factory pool described in this manifest carries the factory's initialization-only guard and the network trading fee; it and any other hookless ETH/ADAM pool pay nothing to the Treasury. This is a platform constraint (no custom hook on the launch pool, no swap callbacks in the guard) that the manifest cannot change and the README discloses; frontends must pin the hooked PoolKey recorded at the owner's post-launch deployment for fee-bearing trades. Holders must approve and stake ADAM in AdamDistributor to earn IMD and PNKSTR, then call claim(), unstake() or exit(); ordinary wallet transfers do not update rewards. Fixed exclusions are zero, dead, Distributor, ADAM, PoolManager and both reward tokens; Hook and Treasury are not explicit exclusions, and neither can stake. The pool entry uses the permitted native-ETH pair, fee 3000, spacing 60 and decimal sqrtPriceX96 2^96; the deployer derives the effective opening price from policy, and these values do not reproduce the manual script's fee-0 hooked pool or its opening tick. The factory supplies its guard, LP and MerkleDistributor, which are not application entries. Notes authorize no initialization calls, script execution or policy changes.
